name: FT232RL
full_name: USB to UART/serial bridge with integrated clock and EEPROM
description: Single-chip USB 2.0 full-speed to UART bridge that handles the entire USB protocol on-chip, requiring no external crystal (integrated clock) and no external configuration ROM (internal EEPROM). It provides a full UART with modem-control and handshake lines, plus five configurable CBUS pins for TX/RX LED drives, clock output, or bit-bang I/O. An internal 3.3 V LDO (3V3OUT) powers the USB transceiver, while VCCIO sets the logic I/O voltage (1.8-5.25 V). Hugely popular on serial adapters and Arduino-style boards thanks to FTDI's mature VCP/D2XX drivers.

extra.3v3out: internal LDO, up to 50 mA external

typical_application: USB-to-serial cable/adapter or on-board programming/console UART; VCCIO tied to the target logic rail (3.3 V via 3V3OUT or 5 V via VCC) to match TXD/RXD levels.
gotchas: counterfeit FT232RL chips are rampant - FTDI drivers have in the past bricked or zeroed the PID of clones; buy from reputable sources
TEST (pin 26) must be tied to GND or the device appears to fail - a very common board bug
VCCIO sets the I/O voltage: do not assume 3.3 V - if VCCIO is tied to 5 V the UART pins swing 5 V and can damage 3.3 V targets
internal clock needs VCC >= 4.0 V (e.g. USB 5 V); running the core at 3.3 V requires an external crystal/oscillator
3V3OUT is an output, not an input - do not feed external 3.3 V into it; decouple with 100 nF
CBUS pins default to TX/RX LED etc. and require the FTDI EEPROM utility (FT_PROG) to reconfigure
